description:
Look at sound: a spectrogram of media or of a score as an image, time left to right, pitch bottom to top on a musical scale with note names up the side, brighter is louder. With a score_id, or a tempo you give, bar and beat lines are drawn. Up to 60 s an image. Low notes sit at the bottom, a voice in the middle, hiss and cymbals at the top; a held note is a level line, a hit is a vertical one. Comes inline and with a signed download url.
One row per semitone from C1 (32.7 Hz) to B9 (15.8 kHz), A4 = 440 Hz; brightness is the level in dBFS from -90 dB (black) to 0 (a full-scale sine), the same scale on every picture. Low rows trade time detail for pitch (a window of 0.92 s at C2, 0.23 s at C4, 28.667 ms at C7); the result gives each octave's window, the plot's pixel box, and where each bar line is. Drawn on the same axes as render.notes.

beats_per_bar.description: Beats in a bar, with tempo: bar lines are drawn and numbered. Without it, beat lines only

first_bar_seconds.description: Where bar 1 starts in the media, with tempo. Default 0

long_edge.description: Longest side (the width) in pixels; rows get taller with it

media_id.description: Media to draw. One of media_id or score_id

score_id.description: A score to render and draw

tempo.description: Beats per minute, to draw bar and beat lines on media

until_seconds.description: End of the range. Up to 60 s after the start. Default the end, or 60 s after the start if that comes first

name: render.spectrogram

x.description: Image pixel column of the line

beat_lines.description: Beat lines drawn (none when closer than 4 pixels)

peak_db.description: Loudest row level in the picture

plot.description: The plot in image pixels: a time t is at x = left + (t - from_seconds) / seconds_per_pixel; a row is row_pixels high, the highest at top

window_seconds.description: Window length at each C: the time detail of that octave

title: Render spectrogram
